newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Cowie shares may fall to 295p.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Cowie shares may fall to 295p.

text.p: The share price of motor retailer Cowie Group may deteriorate over the medium-term, technical analysts said.

Reasons for this include the completion of a bearish chart pattern, the alignment of its medium and long-term moving averages and weakness in the stock's relative strength compared with the All-Share index.

"The share price has fallen below support at 350p completing a large head-and-shoulders top extending back 12 months," said Richard Marshall, a director at Investment Research of Cambridge Ltd. "The implied target is 295p."
By 1030 GMT, Cowie shares were down 4-1/2p at 338-1/2p.

The head-and-shoulders pattern on a daily price chart of Cowie consists of a prominent peak made by the share price when they reached 443p in January and which is flanked on either side by lower peaks. The pattern was completed once neckline support at 350p had been broken earlier this month.

An inspection of Cowie's share price since 1996 indicates the next major chart support is now at 295p -- this had been a support level in February 1996. But the stock's 25-day moving average gave warning of the share price demise when it fell below the 200 day average in May, analysts said.
As a result, the stock's 200 day moving average may be about to head lower -- indicating a weak share price trend -- after having been flat over the past three months, said Marshall.

"The action has been confirmed by the (stock's) relative strength ratio which has broken its long-term uptrend," he added, noting that since their peak in May, the shares have lost 23.7 percent of their value compared with a gain of 8.5 percent by the All-Share index.
"After a two year bull market run, Cowie now looks ready for a correction in front of interim results due at the end of this month," said Marshall.
Cowie Group shares are in the FTSE Mid-250 index.
